# Exit codes are honest: refuse to resume a finished run, nonzero exit on failed apply

## What to build

Fix two Jira bugs about exit codes and `--resume`:

- **KAN-69 / GE-08: a failed final apply still exits 0.** When the last step (applying `graph/<run-id>` to the starting branch as uncommitted changes, `mergeResult` in `src/runner/run.ts` lines 592–613) fails, the run logs `not applied to main: <reason>`, the summary shows a `Not applied to main` section, but `pass()` (lines 452–535) still returns `exitCode: 0`, the summary says `exit code 0 (clean)`, and `endStatus` (lines 94–100) saves run status `done`. Reproduced on this branch with the fake provider: an untracked `2.txt` in the checkout makes the apply roll back (`git merge failed and was rolled back: ... untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge: 2.txt`) and the CLI exits 0.
- **KAN-65 / GE-04: `--resume` on an already-finished run runs again.** `--resume` (`resume()` in `src/runner/run.ts` lines 209–245, after `preflightResume` in `src/launch/preflight.ts` lines 140–167, which picks the run with `findRun` in `src/state/resume.ts` lines 20–33) never looks at the saved run status. On a run whose status is `applied`, it sets the status back to `running` (line 228), redoes the review-phase tail and squash-merges the result into the checkout a second time; when that second apply fails (the files are already there) it still exits 0. Reproduced on this branch: a clean run (exit 0, applied), then `graph-execution --resume` prints `applying graph/<id> to main` / `not applied to main: ... would be overwritten by merge: 1.txt 2.txt` and exits 0.

After the fix:
1. A failed apply (the user wanted the result applied and `applyToCheckout` refused or rolled back) ends the run as an abort: exit code **2** (`EXIT_ABORT`), run status `failed`, the shared abort message `aborted at apply to <target>: not applied to <target>: <reason>` and `to resume: graph-execution --resume --run <id>`. Resuming such a run is allowed and only retries the apply (all tasks are merged and the review phase is saved as `done`, so no agent runs again).
2. `--resume` of a run whose saved status is `applied` or `done` is refused before anything happens (no lock, no reconcile, no agents, no apply), with a `UsageError` whose message contains `already finished`; the CLI prints `error: <message>` and exits 2.

Unchanged on purpose: a result that is *deliberately* not applied because the code review was not performed (`mergeResult(target, unreviewed=true)`, logged as `not applying to <target>: the code review was not performed`) keeps exit code 0 and status `done` (README: "If it was the code reviewer that gave up, the result is not applied to your branch automatically"), and `--no-merge` runs are unchanged. Exit-code convention (`src/state/errors.ts` lines 3–17, README "Exit codes"): 0 success, 1 review loop exhausted, 2 abort or startup failure (resumable), 3 `--web` hand-off blocked. `src/cli.ts` sets the code only through `setExitCode` (lines 50–53) from the `RunResult.exitCode` (lines 221–231) or, for a thrown error, `exitCodeFor(err)` in `main` (lines 353–368), which maps every error to 2.

Another task concurrently edits `src/runner/run.ts` around lines 779–851 (setup/validate interruption). Keep this task's `run.ts` edits to `endStatus` (94–100) if needed and the apply block in `pass()` (506–525); do not touch lines 750–852.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/state/errors.ts` (lines 1–52) — exit code constants, `AbortRunError(message, { step, hint })`, `InterruptedError`, `exitCodeFor`.
- `src/cli.ts` (lines 46–53, 131–155, 183–232, 353–368) — how results and errors become exit codes (`setExitCode`, `serveWeb`, the root action's `--resume` branch, `main`'s catch → `console.error("error: ...")` + `exitCodeFor`).
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 85–100) — `PassOutcome` and `endStatus` (error → `failed`/`aborted`; `merge.ok` → `applied`; `dropped` or exit 0 → `done`; else `failed`).
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 352–449) — the pass/retry loop: after the loop, `endStatus` is saved (420–423), task branches are deleted only for `applied`/`done` (424–433), and `if (last.error !== undefined) { await abortRun(last.error, ...); return { exitCode: await finish("aborted", ctx), ... } }` (436–439).
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 452–535) — `pass()`: review phase, `finish("success")` removes worktrees (507–509), the apply (513–517), `runEnd(...)` (518–524), the returned outcome (525), and the catch that returns `{ exitCode, error }` (526–529).
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 537–558) — `retryTargets`: a failed apply already shows the merge node as failed, so with a retry hub (TTY) the merge node is offered for retry; keep that working.
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 592–613) — `mergeResult`: `unreviewed` → `{ ok: false, reason: "the code review was not performed; ..." }`; `applyToCheckout` failure → `{ ok: false, reason }`.
- `src/runner/run.ts` (lines 203–245) — `resume()`, which calls `preflight({ resume: true, ... })` first (line 211).
- `src/launch/preflight.ts` (lines 19, 140–167) — `UsageError` and `preflightResume`: load the state (149–150), then the hash check (152–159). The refusal goes here so the CLI `--resume`, `--resume --web` (`src/launch/launch.ts:59` calls `preflight`) and `resume()` all get it.
- `src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (lines 195–205) — the existing refusal for a finished suite: `if (store.state.status === "applied" || store.state.status === "done") throw new UsageError(\`suite ${suiteId} already finished\`);` — mirror it.
- `src/state/state.ts` (line 21) — `runStatusSchema = z.enum(["running", "applied", "done", "failed", "aborted"])`.
- `src/ui/Summary.tsx` (lines 47–113) — the summary: exit code ≠ 0/1 renders `Run <id> aborted at <abort.step>: <abort.message>` with the resume hint as next step; the `Not applied to <target>` section comes from `end.merge`.
- `src/runner/run-apply.test.ts` (whole file) — apply tests; lines 60–68 ("does not apply when the user switched branches") and 159–167 ("does not let git overwrite an untracked file") are failed applies; 169–179 is the unreviewed case that must stay exit 0.
- `src/launch/preflight.test.ts` (lines 1–32, 67–96) — `refuses(...)` helper and the hand-built `StateStore` used for resume preflight tests.
- `src/state/resume.test.ts` (lines 1–33, 96–120) and `src/__fixtures__/resume.ts` (lines 54–64, 89–128) — CLI-level resume tests (they run `dist/cli.js`; vitest's global setup runs `npm run build`).
- `src/runner/run-retry.test.ts` (lines 117–132, 165–200) — retry with a failed apply, and the `run status` tests.
- `README.md` (lines 423–446) — "Exit codes" table and "Resume" section to update.

## Patterns to follow

**Refusing a finished run (`src/suite/orchestrator.ts:203-205`):**
```typescript
if (store.state.status === "applied" || store.state.status === "done") {
  throw new UsageError(`suite ${suiteId} already finished`);
}
```

**Abort error with step and hint (`src/state/errors.ts:27-37`, used e.g. `src/runner/run.ts:791-794`):**
```typescript
throw new AbortRunError(`setup command \`${result.command}\` failed with exit code ${result.exitCode}`, {
  step,
  hint: resumeCommand(ctx.runId),
});
```
`AbortRunError`, `EXIT_ABORT`, `resumeCommand` and `codeReviewSkipped` are already imported in `run.ts` (lines 30–38, 52).

**Outcome with an error (`src/runner/run.ts:526-529`):** `runEnd(exitCodeFor(err), lastReports, err); ... return { exitCode: exitCodeFor(err), error: err };` — an outcome with `error` makes `endStatus` return `failed` and the end of `execute()` call `abortRun` (prints `aborted at <step>: <message>`, `state, worktrees and logs are kept in ...`, `to resume: <hint>`) and return `finish("aborted")` = 2.

**Test patterns:** `runDiamond(provider, undefined, { events })` + `ends(events)` in `src/runner/run-apply.test.ts:12-30`; `refuses(opts, /message/, UsageError)` in `src/launch/preflight.test.ts:24-32`; CLI tests via `start(repo)` / `resumeCli(repo, args)` returning execa results with `exitCode`, `stdout`, `stderr` (`src/__fixtures__/resume.ts:54-64`).

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `src/runner/run.ts` — `pass()` apply block (lines 506–525)

- **IMPLEMENT**: After `const merge = ... await mergeResult(mergeTarget, codeReviewSkipped(review.reports)) ...` (513–516), detect a real apply failure: `const applyFailed = merge !== undefined && !merge.ok && !codeReviewSkipped(review.reports);`. When it is true, build `const err = new AbortRunError(\`not applied to ${merge.target}: ${merge.reason ?? "unknown reason"}\`, { step: \`apply to ${merge.target}\`, hint: resumeCommand(ctx.runId) });`, call `runEnd(EXIT_ABORT, review.reports, err, merge, review.human && { decision: review.human.decision, openFindings: review.human.openFindings })` and `return { exitCode: EXIT_ABORT, error: err, merge };`. Otherwise keep the existing `runEnd(...)` and `return` (518–525) unchanged.
- **PATTERN**: the catch at `run.ts:526-529` (outcome with `error`), `AbortRunError` usage at `run.ts:791-794`.
- **IMPORTS**: none new.
- **GOTCHA**: Do not throw: `pass()` must never throw. Do not use `InterruptedError` (that would set status `aborted` and skip `retryTargets`). The worktrees were already removed by `finish("success")` at 507–509; that is fine, `--resume`'s `reconcile` re-adds the integration worktree, and the saved review phase is `done`, so a resume only re-applies. `endStatus` (94–100) then returns `failed` because `last.error` is set — no change needed there, but verify it; keep `applied` only for `merge.ok`. Task branches are then kept (424–433 only delete for `applied`/`done`), which is right for a resumable run. `mergeUnfinished` (565–569, the "Merge as it is" button) is unchanged: it keeps the failure's exit code.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src/runner/run-apply.test.ts src/runner/run-retry.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/launch/preflight.ts` — `preflightResume` (lines 140–167)

- **IMPLEMENT**: Right after `const { state } = store;` (line 150) and before the hash check, add: `if (state.status === "applied" || state.status === "done") { throw new UsageError(\`cannot resume run ${state.runId}: it already finished (${state.status}); the result is on ${state.integrationBranch}\`); }`. Keep the message containing `already finished`.
- **PATTERN**: `src/suite/orchestrator.ts:203-205`.
- **IMPORTS**: none (`UsageError` is defined in this file at line 19).
- **GOTCHA**: `state.status` is optional in the schema (older state files have none): only the two finished values are refused; `running`, `failed`, `aborted` and missing still resume. `cli.ts` `main` prints `error: <message>` to stderr and `exitCodeFor` gives 2 for any error, so no CLI change is needed. The suite only resumes features whose run did not end `done`, so suites are unaffected.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/runner/run-apply.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: (a) In "does not apply when the user switched branches during the run" (60–68) change `expect(result.exitCode).toBe(0)` to `toBe(2)` and assert the run state is `failed` (read `path.join(ctx.runDir, "state.json")` with `readState` from `../__fixtures__/run-diamond.js`; `runDiamond` returns `ctx`) and that `seen[0]!.exitCode` is 2 and `seen[0]!.abort` matches `{ step: "apply to main", hint: expect.stringContaining("--resume") }`. (b) In "does not let git overwrite an untracked file of the user's" (159–167) add `expect(result.exitCode).toBe(2)` (destructure `result`). (c) Add a regression test `it("exits 2, keeps the run resumable and logs the abort when the apply fails", ...)`: put an untracked `2.txt` in `repo` before `runDiamond`, expect exit 2, `lines` (from `../__fixtures__/run-diamond.js`) to include a line starting with `aborted at apply to main: not applied to main:` and `to resume: graph-execution --resume --run ${ctx.runId}`, and state status `failed`. (d) Leave "does not apply a result whose code review was not performed" (169–179) expecting exit 0.
- **PATTERN**: `src/runner/run-apply.test.ts:159-167`.
- **IMPORTS**: `readState`, `lines` from `../__fixtures__/run-diamond.js`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/runner/run-apply.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: Add `it("refuses --resume of a run that already finished", ...)`: for each of `"applied"` and `"done"`, save a `StateStore` exactly like lines 70–89 but with `status` set (hashes computed from the real files so the hash check would pass), then expect `preflight({ cwd: repo, resume: true })` to reject with a `UsageError` whose message matches `/already finished/`. Also assert a `failed` run is not refused for that reason (it may fail later for another reason, e.g. a missing tasks folder; just check the message does not match `/already finished/`).
- **PATTERN**: `src/launch/preflight.test.ts:69-96`.
- **IMPORTS**: already imported (`StateStore`, `computeHashes`, `initialReviewState`, `UsageError`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/launch/preflight.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/state/resume.test.ts` and `src/__fixtures__/resume.ts` (CLI regression + keep existing tests valid)

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - Add to `describe("resume")` in `src/state/resume.test.ts`: `it("refuses to resume a run that already finished, and changes nothing", () => withRepo(undefined, {}, async (repo) => { ... }))`: `start(repo)` exits 0; record `git status --porcelain` and the state file contents; `rm(repo.calls, { force: true })`; `resumeCli(repo)` exits 2, `stderr` contains `already finished`, `stdout` does not contain `applying`; `readCalls(repo)` is empty; `git status --porcelain` and the state's `status` (`applied`) are unchanged.
  - Add `it("resumes a run whose apply failed and only applies it", ...)`: write an untracked `2.txt` into `repo.dir` before `start(repo)`; expect exit 2 and state status `failed`; delete `2.txt`; `rm(repo.calls)`; `resumeCli(repo)` exits 0, state status `applied`, `readCalls` contains no `task:`, `reviewer:` or `tester:` calls, and `git status --porcelain` lists `1.txt`..`4.txt` as untracked.
  - Existing test "lets git win: a merged task whose merge commit is gone ..." (lines 97–120) resumes a run that ended `applied` and whose result is already in the checkout. Keep its intent: before `resumeCli`, rewrite the run's `state.json` with `status: "aborted"` (`await writeFile(path.join(runDir, "state.json"), JSON.stringify({ ...state, status: "aborted" }, null, 2))`) and call `resumeCli(repo, ["--no-merge"])` so the second apply does not collide with the first one's files (it would now correctly exit 2).
  - `killAndResume` in `src/__fixtures__/resume.ts` (89–128): a kill at the final status save leaves `before.status === "applied"`. Right after reading `before`, add: if `before.status === "applied" || before.status === "done"`, run `resumeCli(repo)`, expect `exitCode` 2 and `stderr` to contain `already finished`, and `return true`. Update the comment at lines 118–121 (the "kill after the result was applied" case is now refused instead of re-applied).
- **PATTERN**: `src/state/resume.test.ts:16-33` (CLI refusal tests), `src/__fixtures__/resume.ts:89-128`.
- **IMPORTS**: `writeFile`, `rm` from `node:fs/promises` (already imported in `resume.test.ts`); `readState`, `readCalls`, `onlyRun` from `../__fixtures__/resume.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: These tests run `dist/cli.js`; `npx vitest run` rebuilds it via `vitest.global-setup.ts`. `src/state/resume-kill.test.ts` is slow (up to 10 min); run it once at the end.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/state/resume.test.ts && npx vitest run src/state/resume-kill.test.ts`

### UPDATE `README.md` (lines 423–446)

- **IMPLEMENT**: In the "Exit codes" table, row `0`: replace "The result is applied to your branch as uncommitted changes unless something stopped it" with wording that it is applied unless `--no-merge`, a human Drop, or a code review that was not performed kept it on its branch; row `2`: add "the final apply to your branch failed (`--resume` retries only the apply)". In "Resume", add a bullet: "A run that already finished (status `applied` or `done`) is refused: `cannot resume run <id>: it already finished`, exit code 2."
- **VALIDATE**: `grep -n "already finished" README.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A run whose final apply fails (e.g. untracked file in the way, branch switched, conflicting commits with local changes) exits **2**, saves run status `failed`, logs `aborted at apply to <target>: not applied to <target>: <reason>` and `to resume: graph-execution --resume --run <id>`, and its summary reads `exit code 2 (aborted)` with the `Not applied to <target>` section.
- [ ] Resuming that run re-applies only (no task, reviewer or tester agent runs) and exits 0 with status `applied` once the obstacle is gone.
- [ ] A result not applied because the code review was not performed still exits 0 with status `done`; `--no-merge` runs still exit 0 with status `done`.
- [ ] `graph-execution --resume [--run <id>]` (and `--resume --web`) on a run with status `applied` or `done` exits 2 with stderr `error: cannot resume run <id>: it already finished (<status>); ...`, takes no lock, runs no agent, does not touch the checkout and leaves `state.json` unchanged.
- [ ] Runs with status `running`, `failed`, `aborted` or no status still resume as before.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npx vitest run src/runner/run-apply.test.ts src/runner/run-retry.test.ts src/launch/preflight.test.ts src/state/resume.test.ts src/state/resume-kill.test.ts src/cli.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
# Type / lint
npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint .

# Tests for this slice (vitest's global setup runs `npm run build` first)
npx vitest run src/runner/run-apply.test.ts src/runner/run-retry.test.ts src/runner/run.test.ts src/launch/preflight.test.ts src/state/resume.test.ts src/cli.test.ts src/web/web-retry.test.ts
npx vitest run src/state/resume-kill.test.ts
```
